stem:
Farai keeps these records for a 3.5 ha maize field.

| Item | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Natural region | IIb, near Chinhoyi |
| Planting date | 12 December (first effective rains on 20 November) |
| Spacing | 90 cm × 25 cm, one plant per station |
| Top dressing | Ammonium nitrate at 250 kg/ha |
| Problems seen | Ragged leaves with frass in the funnel in January; long grey rectangular leaf spots in February |
| Grain harvested | 16,800 kg from 3.5 ha |

Fertiliser is sold in 50 kg bags.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the maturity group of cultivar Farai should have chosen for planting as late as 12 December.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the plant population per hectare, to the nearest whole plant.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of bags of ammonium nitrate needed. Round UP to whole bags.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the grain yield in t/ha.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Which problem caused the long grey rectangular leaf spots in February?

options.rationale: Armyworm gave the ragged leaves and frass.
This gives yellowing from the leaf tip along the midrib.

parts.explanation: Grey, rectangular lesions limited by the veins are typical of grey leaf spot.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why planting on 12 December probably reduced Farai's yield.

points.description: The crop missed about three weeks of the season, so it had less time to grow and fill grain.
It was more likely to meet drought at grain filling as the rains ended / more pest pressure / nitrogen released early was leached.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** ways Farai could reduce grey leaf spot next season.

points.description: Rotate maize with a non-host crop such as a legume.
Grow a resistant cultivar / bury or destroy infected residues / spray an approved fungicide when needed.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Describe and explain how Farai should manage his next maize crop, from land preparation to storage, to obtain a higher yield.

points.description: Prepare land early (plough after harvest or prepare basins), lime acid soil and keep a mulch where possible, so planting is not delayed.
Choose a cultivar of suitable maturity and disease resistance for region IIb.
Plant with the first effective rains at about 25 kg/ha and the recommended spacing, so the crop uses the full season.
Apply a basal compound at planting beside (not touching) the seed, for phosphorus and early root growth.
Top dress ammonium nitrate in split doses at about knee height and before tasselling, on moist soil, to reduce leaching.
Weed in the first six to eight weeks, when competition reduces yield most.
Scout weekly for fall armyworm and stalk borer and treat when thresholds are reached; control grey leaf spot by rotation and resistant cultivars.
Harvest after the black layer forms, dry to about 12.5% moisture, treat or use hermetic bags and store off the floor in a clean, rat-proof store.

explanation: Interpret maize records, calculate population, fertiliser and yield, and plan improved management.
hints: For the long part, follow the season in order and give reasons.

stem: Sipho will grow 4 ha of soya beans near Bindura on land that has carried maize for several years but never soya. He will sow 90 kg/ha of seed. Assume one sachet of inoculant treats 60 kg of seed. Last year a neighbour harvested 9,800 kg of soya from 4 ha.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the bacteria in the inoculant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the mass of seed needed, in kg.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of sachets of inoculant needed. Round UP.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the neighbour's yield in t/ha, to two decimal places.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Why must the soya be harvested promptly once the pods are dry?

options.content: Dry soya seed loses its oil within a day
options.rationale: Oil is not lost like this.

options.content: The plants start to grow new pods
options.rationale: Mature soya does not regrow pods.

options.content: Dry pods shatter and drop their seed

parts.explanation: Shattering losses rise quickly when harvest is delayed.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State **two** precautions Sipho must take when inoculating the seed.

points.description: Mix inoculant with seed in the shade, out of the sun.
Plant the same day; keep inoculated seed away from fertiliser and incompatible seed dressings / store inoculant cool.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Explain how the soya will benefit the maize Sipho grows next season.

points.description: Soya residues and roots release fixed nitrogen as they decompose, so the maize needs less nitrogen fertiliser.
As a different family it breaks the cycle of maize pests and diseases (and witchweed).

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Describe and explain how Sipho should grow the soya crop, from land preparation to marketing.

points.description: Prepare a firm, fine-to-medium seedbed on well-drained soil; lime if acid, because nodulation is poor in acid soil.
Apply a basal fertiliser supplying phosphorus and potassium with little nitrogen, because nodules supply nitrogen.
Inoculate seed in the shade and plant the same day into moist soil, in rows about 45 cm apart, at the start of the rains.
Weed early, because young soya competes poorly.
Scout for rust, pod-sucking bugs and red spider mite and spray approved chemicals when needed.
Harvest when leaves have dropped and pods rattle, promptly to avoid shattering.
Thresh, clean and dry to a safe moisture content and store in a dry, clean store.
Market through a contract or buyer (oil and stock-feed processors), grading and keeping records of costs and sales.

stem: Chipo will grow cabbages on a plot 24 m × 13.5 m near Mutare at 60 cm × 45 cm. She will raise 20% more seedlings than she needs in a nursery bed. She expects 90% of the heads to be marketable at an assumed price of US\$0.55 each.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the branch of horticulture to which cabbage production belongs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of cabbage plants on the plot.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of seedlings she should raise.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate her expected income, in US dollars.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: When is the best time of day to transplant the seedlings?

options.content: Early in a hot, windy morning
options.rationale: Wind and heat increase water loss.

options.content: Any time; it makes no difference

options.rationale: Correct: less heat and evaporation overnight.

parts.explanation: Transplanting in the cool reduces wilting while roots re-establish.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why the seedlings are hardened off before transplanting.

points.description: Reducing water and removing shade toughens the seedlings.
So they survive the shock of transplanting and field conditions with less wilting.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Name **two** pests of cabbage and give a control measure for each.

points.description: Diamondback moth / cutworms: approved insecticide when scouting shows damage / collars and digging out cutworms.
Aphids: approved insecticide or natural enemies; remove badly infested plants.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Describe how Chipo should prepare a nursery bed, raise the seedlings and transplant them, giving reasons.

points.description: Choose a sheltered, well-drained site near water where brassicas were not grown recently (soil-borne disease).
Dig deeply, remove stones and weeds, add rotted compost and rake to a fine tilth in a raised bed about 1 m wide.
Sterilise the soil (burning trash or solarisation) to kill damping-off fungi, pests and weed seeds.
Sow thinly in shallow drills, cover lightly and mulch until germination, then remove mulch and give light shade.
Water gently morning and evening; thin crowded seedlings; control pests.
Harden off for one to two weeks by reducing water and shade.
Water the bed before lifting; lift with soil on the roots, holding leaves; transplant in the late afternoon at 60 cm × 45 cm.
Firm, water immediately, shade if hot and replace any that die (gapping).
